AK-2025-HJR45.aiSummary: The Alaska Legislature would urge the U.S. Congress to fully fund the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, which helps pay for special education for students with disabilities. It says federal funding should reach at least 40% of the average per-student cost and stay at that level. The resolution affects students with disabilities, schools, families, and school districts in Alaska.

AK-2025-HJR38.aiSummary: This resolution would urge the U.S. Congress to recognize public safety telecommunicators, like 911 dispatchers, as first responders. It would also urge Congress to pass the Enhancing First Response Act, which would reclassify them as a protective service job. The resolution says this group plays a key role in emergency response and that the change could affect the benefits and support they can get.

AK-2025-HB48.aiSummary: The bill would change how Alaska’s civil legal services fund is financed. It would let lawmakers put into the fund up to 25 percent of court filing fees from the prior year, and the fund could be used to pay groups that provide civil legal help to low-income people. A low-income person is defined as someone with income at or below 125 percent of the federal poverty level for Alaska.

AK-2025-HB27.aiSummary: The bill would require the state education department to set up hands-only CPR lessons for public school students and decide which grade levels must get them. AK-2025-HB13.aiSummary: The bill would let Alaska cities and towns give optional property tax breaks for certain homes and rental properties, including places used by volunteer fire, emergency medical, paramedic, and hazardous materials responders. It also covers some long-term rental units, mobile home parks, homes rented to low-income families, a person’s main home, and homes bought by first-time buyers. AK-2025-SCR203.title: Suspending Rules 24(c), 35, 41(b), and 42(e), Uniform Rules of the Alaska State Legislature, concerning House Bill No. 381, relating to the taxation of certain natural gas project property and related facilities; relating to local contributions for public school funding; relating to municipal property taxes; relating to the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation; relating to reporting requirements for natural gas pipeline projects; relating to approval of contracts by the Regulatory Commission of Alaska and inflation adjustment of the maximum price of natural gas; relating to an alternative volumetric tax on natural gas throughput; relating to agreements and a payment related to a natural gas project; and relating to municipal impact grants.
AK-2025-SCR203.aiSummary: The resolution would suspend certain Alaska legislative rules for House Bill 381 so its title can be changed as it moves forward. The bill deals with taxes and fees tied to a natural gas project, school funding, city property taxes, the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation, pipeline reporting, contract approval, gas price limits, and municipal impact grants. The Senate passed the resolution and sent it to the House.

AK-2025-SB3001.title: An Act relating to the taxation of certain natural gas project property and related facilities; relating to local contributions for public school funding; relating to municipal property taxes; relating to the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation and funds of the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation; relating to reporting requirements for natural gas pipeline projects; creating the Alaska affordable heating fuel fund; relating to approval of contracts by the Regulatory Commission of Alaska and inflation adjustment of the maximum price of natural gas; relating to an alternative volumetric tax on natural gas throughput; relating to a municipal impact grant program and fund; relating to agreements and a payment related to a natural gas project; and providing for an effective date.
AK-2025-SB3001.aiSummary: The bill would change taxes and reporting tied to a major natural gas project in Alaska. It would also affect how local school funding is counted, how municipal property taxes work, and how the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation handles some funds. It would create an Alaska affordable heating fuel fund and a municipal impact grant program, and it would set rules for certain contracts, gas price limits, and an alternative tax on natural gas throughput.
